o: An element is good if it is strictly greater than the elements k positions to its left and right, when those exist. With n <= 100 we simply check each index directly. In Example 1 (k = 2), nums[1]=3 beats nums[3]=1, nums[4]=5 beats nums[2]=2, and nums[5]=4 has no right neighbor and beats nums[3]=1, so the answer is 3+5+4=12.
k: Direct O(n) check per index is sufficient given n <= 100.
Strictly greater comparison; missing neighbors impose no constraint.

a.i: For each index i verify nums[i] > nums[i-k] (if i-k >= 0) and nums[i] > nums[i+k] (if i+k < n), accumulating matches.

w: Trivial problem; the only mistakes are boundary handling (missing neighbor means no constraint) and using >= instead of strict >.
